notes: Settlement 2026-11-07: reliefs pension exclusion covers public_pension_other_state: A put it in covers_unclear, B in covers; the sources' wording settles it for covers, with no paying_states. njit6 (Taxable Retirement Income): 'Taxable pensions include all state and local government, teachers', and federal pensions ... However, if you (and/or your spouse/civil union partner if filing jointly) were 62 or older or disabled, you may be able to use the retirement exclusions to reduce your taxable income.' GIT-1 & 2 p.4: 'State, local government, teachers', and federal pensions are all treated the same as private sector employee pensions and annuities.' Instructions p.15 lists 'Federal, state, and local government, and teachers' pensions' as taxable on line 20a, and p.22: 'You can exclude all or part of the income reported on line 20a'. No source limits 'state' to New Jersey or names a reciprocity rule. Same for the disability-pension entry ('Public or private disability pension benefits').

Settlement 2026-11-07: New York State pension: A and B both found nothing specific; settled the same way. No source names a New York (or any other state's) pension; New York appears only in the credit for taxes paid to other jurisdictions ('Income From New York', Schedule NJ-COJ) and a nonresident example in GIT-1 & 2. A New York State pension of a New Jersey resident falls under 'all state ... pensions' (njit6): taxable on line 20a, with the line 28a exclusion.

Settlement 2026-11-07: reliefs pension exclusion covers roth_conversion: A said covers, B said covers_unclear; covers. GIT-1 & 2 p.18 (Roth IRAs): 'If you convert a traditional IRA to a Roth IRA, any amount from the existing IRA that would be taxable if withdrawn must be included in your income on line 20a'; Instructions p.16 (Roth IRA): 'any amount from the existing IRA that would be taxable if withdrawn must be included on line 20a'; Instructions p.22 Line A of the exclusion is 'Amount from line 20a'. The worksheet line takes it (extraction brief rule 4). The booklet does not say the words 'conversion qualifies for the exclusion'.

Settlement 2026-11-07: pension exclusion split: A wrote one entry (age 62, disability in other_conditions), B two entries (age 62; blind/disabled) with best_of_group and cannot_combine_with. Two entries kept, sharing best_of_group nj_pension_exclusion, because 'age 62 or older or blind/disabled' (Instructions p.22) is an OR test. cannot_combine_with dropped: on a joint return one spouse may qualify by age and the other by disability under the one shared maximum, which a cannot-combine list would forbid.

Settlement 2026-11-07: pension exclusion income_test steps: A gave keep_share 1 in the first band, B gave amount (the cap) there; A's form kept, the dollar maximum is in cap. Bands and shares agree in both and in Instructions p.22, GIT-1 & 2 p.19 and njit7.

Settlement 2026-11-07: pension exclusion vs Worksheet D percentages: both readers saw that the line 28a chart (Instructions p.22) prints the upper bands as '% of line 20a' and the Worksheet D and E 'Maximum Exclusion' charts (p.23, p.24) as '% of line 27'. Recorded as printed: line 20a shares on the pension exclusion (also GIT-1 & 2 p.19 'Multiply your taxable pension found on Line 20a ... by the percentage' and njit7), line 27 shares on the unclaimed exclusion's maximum. GIT-1 & 2 p.25 example applies both in one return (pension 6,200, total income 114,000: pension exclusion 3,100; 'Maximum Exclusion $57,000'), so the two charts are two different rules, not a misprint.

Settlement 2026-11-07: unclaimed exclusion income_test: A said stepped from 100,000 (keep_share of the cap), B said removes over 150,000 with the percentages in cap_rule; B's form kept. Worksheet D (p.23) prints the cliff 'Is income on line 27, NJ-1040 MORE than $150,000? Yes. You are not eligible'; its upper bands are shares of line 27, which a step's keep_share (a share of the relief) cannot hold, so they are in cap_rule.
Settlement 2026-11-07: military pension who.basis: A each_person, B return; each_person (each person's own military pension is exempt 'regardless of your age or disability status', njit6).

Settlement 2026-11-07: Social Security and railroad retirement: A had a railroad-only entry, B one entry covering social_security and railroad_retirement; railroad-only kept, Social Security is held in social_security.treatment (exempt).

Settlement 2026-11-07: capital_gains: A recorded gains from New Jersey and direct federal obligations as exempt (applies_to other), B left capital_gains empty; A's entry kept: Instructions p.10 prints 'Interest and capital gains from (1) obligations of the State of New Jersey ... or (2) direct federal obligations' as exempt income. No other gains preference is printed.

Settlement 2026-11-07: brackets.derivation: neither reader used it. Added with the 2025 Tax Table (PDF p.56-64): a helper parsed all 2,000 printed rows (0 to 100,000) and the bracket schedule reproduces every one at the row midpoint, rounded to the dollar, for both columns. method is tax_table, not formula: the schema's single formula is checked against both the single and the joint schedule, and New Jersey's constants differ by status (see the next note).

Rate schedule formula constants as printed ('Multiply Line 42 by' then 'Subtract'), PDF p.65. Table A (single; married/CU partner separate): 0-20,000 x .014 - 0; 20,000-35,000 x .0175 - 70.00; 35,000-40,000 x .035 - 682.50; 40,000-75,000 x .05525 - 1,492.50; 75,000-500,000 x .0637 - 2,126.25; 500,000-1,000,000 x .0897 - 15,126.25; 1,000,000 and over x .1075 - 32,926.25. Table B (married/CU couple joint; head of household; qualifying widow(er)/surviving CU partner): 0-20,000 x .014 - 0; 20,000-50,000 x .0175 - 70.00; 50,000-70,000 x .0245 - 420.00; 70,000-80,000 x .035 - 1,154.50; 80,000-150,000 x .05525 - 2,775.00; 150,000-500,000 x .0637 - 4,042.50; 500,000-1,000,000 x .0897 - 17,042.50; 1,000,000 and over x .1075 - 34,842.50. Every constant equals the tax the recorded brackets give at the band start, except Table B 70,000-80,000: the bands give 1,155.00 there and the printed 1,154.50 gives 0.50 more tax across that band. The Tax Table follows the bands (row 70,100-70,150 prints 1,299; the formula would give 1,299.88, i.e. 1,300), and taxable income under 100,000 must use the Tax Table ('Use this table if your New Jersey taxable income on line 42 is less than $100,000'), so the constant is never the one applied. Both converters print 1,154.50.

Brackets: the booklet prints two schedules; married_separate repeats Table A and head_of_household repeats Table B because each table is headed with those statuses. Qualifying widow(er)/surviving CU partner also uses Table B. No surtax (10.75% over 1,000,000 is a bracket) and no recapture.

Line 20a covers 'Retirement income such as pensions, annuities, and certain IRA withdrawals' (Instructions p.15), including 401(k), Keogh, 403(b) and 457 distributions over previously taxed contributions (GIT-1 & 2 pp.14-15). The New Jersey taxable amount can be lower than the federal one: contributions to plans other than 401(k) plans (and to IRAs, 403(b) and 457 plans) were taxed when made and are recovered tax-free by the Three-Year Rule, General Rule or IRA Worksheet C (line 20b). That is the taxable base, not a relief, so it has no entry.

Pension exclusion, joint returns: in the upper bands the share applies to the qualifying spouse's pension only (GIT-1 & 2 p.21 example: total income 127,000, qualifying spouse's pension 10,000, 'Applicable Pension Exclusion $2,500' = 25%).

Unclaimed exclusion covers all_income: GIT-1 & 2 p.22-23 'exclude other types of income (wages, interest, dividends, etc.)'; the worksheet puts no income-kind limit on line 9. The amount cannot exceed the qualifying person's income (GIT-1 & 2 p.24 example: maximum 100,000 unused, total income 85,000, unclaimed exclusion 85,000).

Special Exclusion who.basis is return: the age test is 'You (and/or your spouse, if filing jointly) were 62 or older' (GIT-1 & 2 p.26), and the Social Security test applies to both spouses ('neither spouse can claim'), so it is one amount per return.

njit7 also prints the exclusion maximums for 2016 and prior to 2020 ('scheduled increases ... over a four-year period, beginning with Tax Year 2017'); not recorded, as this record is 2025. GIT-1 & 2 (January 2026) says 'Line 20a of the 2024 NJ-1040' in its percentage chart; its amounts match the 2025 instructions.
Nonresidents: njit6 says 'If you are a nonresident, your pension, annuity, and IRA income is not subject to New Jersey Income Tax.' This record is the resident return.

Standard deduction: the booklet prints no standard deduction. Lines 31-37c (medical expenses over 2% of gross income, alimony paid, qualified conservation contribution, health enterprise zone, alternative business calculation, organ donor, NJBEST, NJCLASS, tuition and similar) and the property tax deduction (line 41) or credit are not recorded: not general deductions, and outside the retirement scope.
Indexing: nothing in the instructions, GIT-1 & 2 or the two web pages says any figure is adjusted for inflation (not found in the booklet).

Part-year residents prorate the maximum pension and unclaimed exclusions by months resident (15 days or more counts as a month) when income for the entire year is 100,000 or less; not held in a field.

Format v1 adoption 2026-11-07: nj_unclaimed_pension_exclusion gets earned_income_limit 3,000 per return (Worksheet D lines 4-8, PDF p.23: wages, net profits from business, partnership and S corporation income, lines 15, 18, 21, 22, each entered as nothing when a loss, PDF p.13 and p.18; 'combined if filing jointly', GIT-1 & 2 p.23). The test was already in who.other_conditions and not_covered.

reliefs.label: Pension/Retirement Exclusion (line 28a): age 62 or older
not_covered: Social Security benefits, Railroad Retirement benefits, public or private disability pension benefits until the year you turn 65, and U.S. military pensions and survivor's benefit payments are nontaxable and not reported on line 20a (Instructions p.15)

other_conditions: age 62 or older on the last day of the tax year (December 31 for calendar-year filers)
joint return: only the pension, annuity or IRA withdrawal of a spouse who qualifies is excluded; the filing-status maximum still applies

reliefs.cap_rule: Line 28a is the lesser of Line A (amount from line 20a; joint filers enter only the pension income of a spouse who qualifies) and Line B (the chart amount). With line 27 of $0-$100,000 Line B is the filing-status amount held in cap; from $100,001 to $150,000 it is a percentage of line 20a (income_test steps), so the dollar cap no longer applies; over $150,000 no exclusion. One maximum per return, shared by both spouses: 'you can still claim the maximum pension exclusion. However, you can only exclude the pension, annuity, or IRA withdrawal of the spouse who is 62 or older or disabled' (GIT-1 & 2 p.21). Part-year residents with income for the entire year of $0-$100,000 prorate the maximum by months resident; not prorated over $100,000.

measure.as_printed: Income on line 27, Total Income: 'Add lines 15 through 26 (do not include lines 16b and 20b)' (Instructions p.21); form line 27 'Add lines 15, 16a, 17 through 20a, and 21 through 26'. GIT-1 & 2 and njit7 call it 'total income for the entire year'.
